$comment: ONE FILE, TWO RUNNERS. __tests__/types/quote.test.ts feeds these to isQuoteOpen();
public.is_quote_open(). If the TypeScript mirror and the SQL definition ever
disagree, one of the two suites fails on the case that separates them.
Modelled on lateJobCases.json, which exists because 'late' drifted three ways.
'Open quote' had drifted FOUR ways by 2026-09-09 -- the assistant answered 16, 11
and 6 in one afternoon (ai_chat_messages.tool_trace holds all three queries) and
the dashboard tile had a fourth reading again -- so it gets the same treatment
rather than a comment asking people to keep two files in step.
`today` IS A FIXED ANCHOR, NOT A REAL DATE. isQuoteOpen() reads the machine
clock, so the TypeScript suite re-anchors each expiration_date to the same OFFSET
from the real today; the Python suite passes `today` to the SQL function directly.
That keeps the boundary cases meaningful on any machine, on any day.
EVERY CASE NAMES THE CONDITION IT ISOLATES. A case that would still pass with one
of the three conditions deleted is not pulling its weight.

cases.name: active, unwon, dated in the future — the baseline open quote
expires today — the boundary is inclusive, a quote is live on its last day
expired yesterday — lapsed work must be re-quoted, so it is not in play
no expiration date — an undated quote never lapses
won — converted_at is stamped while status stays 'active'; this is the 16-vs-6 case
status 'expired' — the other half of the enum is never open
won AND lapsed — no condition rescues it
won, undated — converted_at alone closes it
